review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definitions it depends on in Avoid.lean (margin, gridPoint, avoid). I grepped the Besicovitch directory for how avoid is unfolded. Avoid.lean has no simp attributes and no membership lemma for `avoid`. The proofs in this file use ad hoc `simp`/`simp only` calls that I didn't see failing. I found no rewrite-direction problems, competing rules or cycles. The only issue is the missing interface lemma, which is a modest improvement, and I did not run Lean.

findings.problem: `avoid` is a bare `def` with no membership lemma and no simp attribute. To use `x ∉ avoid (L:ℝ) n` the proof has to unfold the definition with `simpa [avoid, ...]` and then push the negation through the binder with `not_forall` and `not_le`. Other files do the same thing: `Avoid.lean` has `unfold avoid` at line 141. Unfolding the definition at use sites leaks its set-builder body, and a later change to `avoid` would break each of these sites.
findings.proposed_change: In `Avoid.lean`, add a lemma `mem_avoid : x ∈ avoid L n ↔ ∀ i : ℤ, margin L n ≤ |x - gridPoint n i|`, proved by `Iff.rfl`, and mark it `@[simp]`. A `@[simp]` lemma is safe here because the left side is a membership in a constant-headed definition, and the right side doesn't mention `avoid`, so it can't loop. Then this call becomes `simpa [not_forall, not_le] using hbad` (or `simpa [mem_avoid] using hbad` if you don't want the attribute). Uses of `avoid` elsewhere can also rewrite with `mem_avoid` instead of `unfold avoid`.
findings.benefit: Callers get the canonical unfolded form `∀ i, margin L n ≤ |x - gridPoint n i|` through the simp set, with no need to unfold `avoid` itself. The simp calls no longer depend on how `avoid` is defined.

evidence.excerpt: def avoid (L : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Set ℝ := {x | ∀ i : ℤ, margin L n ≤ |x - gridPoint n i|}
